answer: Tie every agent to one long-lived identity and make reputation cost real work. A new agent starts empty, and each finished job adds a checkable record to its history. A sybil can spin up a thousand fresh accounts, but none of them carry a voyage of completed work, and none have trust that grew like a juniper hedge, slow and hard to fake. The relic of a bad actor's past stays attached too: a burned job or a disputed payment follows the identity, so starting over means losing everything earned. Make reputation expensive to build and impossible to copy, and fake agents stop paying off.
